messages:
alice: FYI staging push blocked by deploy-bot. Reject reason: manifest list platform-order mismatch + cosign verification failed (fingerprint changed). Anyone around to triage?

deploy-bot: publish_rejected: reason=[manifestlist_platform_array_diff, cosign_sig_invalid]. see: https://deploybot.internal/rejects/4380001234

ben: likely culprit: I toggled BuildKit INLINE_CACHE for cross-arch CI yesterday to speed rebuilds. It can change layer/linking order even if image contents are functionally equal.

carla: quick repro: `skopeo inspect --raw docker://staging.redwood.io/svc:canary | jq '.manifests[].platform'` vs previous signed manifest. Platform entries are in different order.

ben: confirmed. The blobs are the same, but the manifest bytes differ (order). Cosign signs the exact manifest JSON, so verification fails.

erin: security: we can't accept unsigned or manually re-tagged manifests into prod without KMS-backed attestation and an approval flow. Manual override is only for emergencies with audit.

dan: change window starts in 40m. We should decide: either rollback the canary to the last pinned digest or rebuild without INLINE_CACHE and re-sign. Rollback safe path.

gina: ops + SRE preference: rollback canary to last-good digest immediately and block further publishes from this branch until CI fix. Then rebuild and re-publish.

alice: options: (A) rollback canary to sha256:deadbeef... now, then rebuild no-inline-cache and sign; (B) apply a manifest canonicalizer step before signing (fast but adds complexity); (C) emergency KMS attestation (requires ops + security). Thoughts?

ben: rebuild w/o inline cache is clean, takes ~15-22m for multi-arch CI. I can trigger with `CI_NO_INLINE_CACHE=1 ./ci/build-push-multiarch.sh --cosign`

carla: I'm wary of adding canonicalizer; prefer deterministic builds. I'll open INFRA ticket to add a manifest-stability check pre-sign: INFRA-5462.

erin: if we go the KMS attestation route we need a ticket and justification recorded. Not a good pattern for routine fixes.

alice: decision: immediate rollback of canary to pinned digest, block this branch for further publishes, ben will rebuild without inline cache and re-sign. Postmortem to include CI flag, INFRA-5462, and a 24h hold on cross-arch pushes.

dan: initiating rollback -> promoting sha256:deadbeef... to canary. Monitoring.

deploy-bot: rollback applied by dan: canary now points to sha256:deadbeef... awaiting health checks.

gina: watching traces and error rates. Will shout if anything spikes.

ben: kicked off rebuild: `CI_NO_INLINE_CACHE=1 ./ci/build-push-multiarch.sh --sign --notify`. ETA ~20m, will paste cosign output when done.

alice: updating release notes: "staging publish blocked due to manifest ordering change from BuildKit inline cache; canary rolled back; rebuild in progress without inline cache; infra ticket created." Also placing a temporary publish freeze for multi-arch for next 24h.

erin: filing audit template just in case (but we shouldn't need manual attestation).

carla: INFRA-5462 created: add manifest equality assert + fail build if non-deterministic.

ben: new build finished, cosign signature: sha256:beefcafe..., running deploy-bot publish-check now.

deploy-bot: publish accepted: manifestlist canonical order verified, cosign verification ok. staging updated.

alice: great work. We'll keep canary at previous level and resume ramp after +30m healthy. Postmortem draft to follow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
